question.text: Which of the following best describes the claim structure of equity shareholders on a company?

answer.text: Priority claim on assets before debt holders
Fixed claim on periodic interest payments
Residual claim on net assets after all liabilities are paid

explanation.text: The Logic: Equity investors have a residual claim on the company's net assets — meaning they receive whatever remains after all liabilities have been paid. They are not entitled to fixed periodic interest or guaranteed dividend payments. The Trap: Equity is not a priority claim ahead of debt, and dividends are not guaranteed. The residual nature of the claim is what distinguishes equity from debt-style instruments. Note: This residual claim is precisely why equity offers higher potential returns but also higher risk — the risk-return tradeoff is built into the claim structure.
